questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is obtained by hydroboration - oxidation of propene?
questions.solution:
Hydroboration-oxidation of an alkene results in the anti-Markovnikov addition of water across the double bond.

Propene ($CH_3-CH=CH_2$) reacts with diborane ($B_2H_6$) to form tripropylborane as an intermediate.

Subsequent oxidation with hydrogen peroxide ($H_2O_2$) in an alkaline medium yields propan-1-ol.

$CH_3-CH=CH_2 \xrightarrow[2. H_2O_2, OH^-]{1. B_2H_6} CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-OH$

Answer: Propan-1-ol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following has lowest boiling point?
questions.solution:
The boiling point of isomeric alcohols decreases with an increase in branching.

As branching increases, the molecule becomes more spherical in shape, which decreases the surface area. A smaller surface area leads to weaker van der Waals forces of attraction between the molecules, thereby lowering the boiling point.

Among the given isomers of butyl alcohol, tert-butyl alcohol is the most branched.

Therefore, tert-butyl alcohol has the lowest boiling point.

Answer: tert-Butyl alcohol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product P obtained in following reaction
questions.solution:
The given reaction is the condensation of phenol with formaldehyde in the presence of an acid catalyst, which is the first step in the synthesis of Bakelite (Lederer-Manasse reaction).

In the presence of an acid, formaldehyde is protonated to generate the electrophile $^+CH_2OH$:
$HCHO + H^+ \rightleftharpoons ^+CH_2OH$

The $-OH$ group of phenol is strongly activating and directs the incoming electrophile to the ortho and para positions.

The electrophile $^+CH_2OH$ attacks the ortho and para positions of the phenol ring, leading to the formation of ortho-hydroxybenzyl alcohol and para-hydroxybenzyl alcohol.

Among the given options, ortho-hydroxybenzyl alcohol is present, which corresponds to the correct product.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Propyne on reaction with water in presence of $40\%$ sulphuric acid and $1\%$ mercuric sulphate forms
questions.solution:
Propyne undergoes hydration in the presence of dilute sulphuric acid and mercuric sulphate according to Markovnikov's rule.

The addition of a water molecule to the triple bond initially yields an unstable enol intermediate, prop-1-en-2-ol.

$CH_3-C \equiv CH + H_2O \xrightarrow{Hg^{2+}, H^+} CH_3-C(OH)=CH_2$

The enol intermediate rapidly undergoes tautomerization to form the more stable keto form, propanone.

$CH_3-C(OH)=CH_2 \rightleftharpoons CH_3-CO-CH_3$

Answer: Propanone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Benzonitrile on reaction with a reagent in dry ether followed by hydrolysis forms benzophenone along with ammonia and hydroxymagnesium bromide. Identify the reagent used in above transformation.
questions.solution:
Benzonitrile ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN}$) reacts with a Grignard reagent to form an imine salt, which on hydrolysis gives a ketone.

Since the product is benzophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COC}_6\text{H}_5$), the Grignard reagent must provide a phenyl group ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5^-$).

The formation of hydroxymagnesium bromide ($\text{Mg(OH)Br}$) as a by-product indicates that the halogen in the Grignard reagent is bromine.

The reaction is:

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN} + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{MgBr} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} (\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)_2\text{C=NMgBr}$

$(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)_2\text{C=NMgBr} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow (\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)_2\text{C=O} + \text{NH}_3 + \text{Mg(OH)Br}$

The reagent used is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the product 'B' in the following reaction
$\text{Isopropyl cyanide} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{SnCl}_2, \text{HCl}}} \text{A} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+}} \text{B} + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$
questions.solution:
The given reaction is Stephen reduction.

Isopropyl cyanide is $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CN}$.

When isopropyl cyanide is treated with $\text{SnCl}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$, it undergoes reduction to form an imine hydrochloride intermediate (A).

$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CN} + 2[\text{H}] + \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{SnCl}_2, \text{HCl}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}=\text{NH}\cdot\text{HCl}$ (A)

Acidic hydrolysis of the imine hydrochloride yields the corresponding aldehyde (B).

$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}=\text{NH}\cdot\text{HCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CHO} + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$

The product B is $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CHO}$, which is 2-methylpropanal.

Answer: 2-Methylpropanal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the reagent 'R' used in the following reaction
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{R}}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO} + \text{HCl}$
questions.solution:
The given reaction is the conversion of benzoyl chloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl}$) to benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$).

This transformation is known as the Rosenmund reduction.

The reagent used for this reaction is hydrogen gas in the presence of a palladium catalyst supported on barium sulfate ($\text{H}_2, \text{Pd}-\text{BaSO}_4$).

The barium sulfate acts as a catalytic poison that partially deactivates the palladium, preventing the further reduction of the newly formed aldehyde into an alcohol.

Thus, the reagent 'R' is $\text{H}_2, \text{Pd}-\text{BaSO}_4$.

Answer: $\text{H}_2, \text{Pd}-\text{BaSO}_4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following statements is NOT correct regarding Hofmann's exhaustive alkylation?
options: In this quaternary ammmonium salts are obtained.
Two moles of alkylhalide when heated with one mole primary amine forms tetraalkyl ammonium halide.
Depending on the quantity of alkyl halides treated with primary amine, the mixture of secondary and tertiary amines obtained.
The reaction is carried out in presence of $\text{NaHCO}_3$
questions.solution:
Hofmann's exhaustive alkylation is the process of converting an amine into a quaternary ammonium salt by treating it with an excess of alkyl halide.

When a primary amine ($RNH_2$) is heated with an alkyl halide ($RX$), it undergoes successive nucleophilic substitution reactions:
$RNH_2 + RX \rightarrow R_2NH + HX$ (Secondary amine)
$R_2NH + RX \rightarrow R_3N + HX$ (Tertiary amine)
$R_3N + RX \rightarrow R_4N^+X^-$ (Quaternary ammonium salt)

To convert one mole of a primary amine into a tetraalkyl ammonium halide, three moles of alkyl halide are required, not two. Therefore, the statement that two moles of alkyl halide form a tetraalkyl ammonium halide is incorrect.

The reaction is typically carried out in the presence of a mild base like $\text{NaHCO}_3$ to neutralize the acid ($HX$) formed, which prevents the protonation of the amine and maintains its nucleophilicity. Depending on the stoichiometric ratio of the reactants, a mixture of secondary and tertiary amines can also be obtained.

Answer: Two moles of alkylhalide when heated with one mole primary amine forms tetraalkyl ammonium halide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following amines does NOT form alkyl isocyanide when heated with alc. KOH and chloroform
questions.solution:
The reaction of an amine with chloroform and alcoholic KOH to form an alkyl isocyanide is known as the carbylamine reaction.

This test is given only by primary (aliphatic and aromatic) amines. Secondary and tertiary amines do not respond to this test.

Methanamine, propan-2-amine, and ethanamine are primary amines, so they will form alkyl isocyanides.

N, N-Diethylethanamine is a tertiary amine, hence it does not undergo the carbylamine reaction and will not form an alkyl isocyanide.

Answer: N, N-Diethylethanamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the total mass of products obtained when one gram mole of sucrose is hydrolysed?
questions.solution:
The chemical equation for the hydrolysis of sucrose is:

$C_{12}H_{22}O_{11} + H_2O \rightarrow C_6H_{12}O_6 + C_6H_{12}O_6$

One mole of sucrose reacts with one mole of water to produce one mole of glucose and one mole of fructose.

Molar mass of glucose ($C_6H_{12}O_6$) = $180\ \text{g/mol}$

Molar mass of fructose ($C_6H_{12}O_6$) = $180\ \text{g/mol}$

Total mass of products = $180 + 180 = 360\ \text{g}$

Answer: $360\ \text{g}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following has largest size?
questions.solution:
The size of the given biological entities generally follows the order: Antibody $\lt $ Virus $\lt $ Bacteria $\lt $ Cancer cell.

Antibodies are protein molecules and are the smallest (around $10$ to $15$ nm).

Viruses are infectious agents composed of genetic material and protein coats, typically ranging from $20$ to $300$ nm.

Bacteria are prokaryotic cells, usually measuring between $1$ to $10\mu$m.

Cancer cells are eukaryotic animal cells, which are the largest among the given options, typically ranging from $10$ to $30\mu$m or more.

Therefore, a cancer cell has the largest size.

Answer: Cancer cell

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is NOT a globular protein?
questions.solution:
Proteins are classified into two types based on their molecular shape: fibrous proteins and globular proteins.

Fibrous proteins have a thread-like structure. Examples include keratin (present in hair, wool, silk) and myosin (present in muscles).

Globular proteins have a spherical shape. Examples include insulin, egg albumin, and serum albumin.

Therefore, keratin is a fibrous protein and not a globular protein.

Answer: Keratin

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify final products in the following sequence of reactions
$\text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{H}^+}} \text{intermediate} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{Ni}, \Delta}}^{\large{\text{H}_2}} \text{Products}$
questions.solution:
The first step is the Fischer esterification reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst. The reaction produces an ester as the intermediate.

$\text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{RCOOR'} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

The intermediate formed is the ester $\text{RCOOR'}$.

The second step involves the catalytic hydrogenation (hydrogenolysis) of the ester using hydrogen gas over a nickel catalyst at high temperature. This process cleaves the ester bond, reducing the acyl group ($\text{RCO}-$) to a primary alcohol and releasing the alkoxy group ($-\text{OR'}$) as another alcohol.

$\text{RCOOR'} + 2\text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni}, \Delta} \text{RCH}_2\text{OH} + \text{R'OH}$

Thus, the final products are $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$ and $\text{R'OH}$.

Answer: $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH} + \text{R'}-\text{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following metal halides have more covalent character?
questions.solution:
According to Fajan's rules, the covalent character of a metal halide increases with an increase in the positive charge on the central metal cation. A higher charge on the cation results in greater polarizing power, which increases the covalent character of the bond.

The oxidation states of the central metal cations in the given options are:
$\text{SnCl}_2$: $+2$
$\text{PbCl}_4$: $+4$
$\text{SbCl}_3$: $+3$
$\text{PbCl}_2$: $+2$

Since $\text{Pb}$ in $\text{PbCl}_4$ has the highest oxidation state of $+4$, the $\text{Pb}^{4+}$ ion has the maximum polarizing power. Thus, $\text{PbCl}_4$ has the most covalent character.

Answer: $\text{PbCl}_4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compound has square pyramidal structure?
questions.solution:
The shape of the molecules can be determined using VSEPR theory by calculating the number of bond pairs (bp) and lone pairs (lp) on the central Xenon (Xe) atom, which has 8 valence electrons.

For $\text{XeF}_4$: Xe forms 4 single bonds with F atoms, using 4 electrons. Remaining electrons = 4 (2 lone pairs). With 4 bp and 2 lp, the hybridization is $sp^3d^2$ and the shape is square planar.

For $\text{XeF}_6$: Xe forms 6 single bonds with F atoms, using 6 electrons. Remaining electrons = 2 (1 lone pair). With 6 bp and 1 lp, the hybridization is $sp^3d^3$ and the shape is distorted octahedral.

For $\text{XeO}_3$: Xe forms 3 double bonds with O atoms, using 6 electrons. Remaining electrons = 2 (1 lone pair). With 3 bp ($\sigma$-bonds) and 1 lp, the hybridization is $sp^3$ and the shape is trigonal pyramidal.

For $\text{XeOF}_4$: Xe forms 1 double bond with O and 4 single bonds with F, using $2 + 4 = 6$ electrons. Remaining electrons = 2 (1 lone pair). With 5 bp ($\sigma$-bonds) and 1 lp, the hybridization is $sp^3d^2$ and the shape is square pyramidal.

Answer: $\text{XeOF}_4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is formal charge on sulphur in sulphuric acid molecule?
questions.solution:
The most stable Lewis structure of sulphuric acid ($H_2SO_4$) minimizes the formal charge by expanding the octet of the central sulphur atom. In this structure, sulphur forms two double bonds with two oxygen atoms and two single bonds with two hydroxyl ($-OH$) groups.

The formula for formal charge is:
Formal charge = (Valence electrons) - (Non-bonding electrons) - $\dfrac{1}{2}$ (Bonding electrons)

For the sulphur atom in $H_2SO_4$:
Number of valence electrons = $6$
Number of non-bonding electrons = $0$
Number of bonding electrons = $12$ (since it forms $6$ bonds)

Formal charge = $6 - 0 - \dfrac{12}{2} = 0$

Answer: $0$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions has of overall order $1.5$ ?
questions.solution:
The thermal decomposition of acetaldehyde is a well-known example of a reaction with a fractional order.

The reaction is: $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}_{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{CH}_{4(g)} + \text{CO}_{(g)}$

The experimentally determined rate law for this reaction is:

$\text{Rate} = k[\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}]^{1.5}$

Thus, the overall order of the reaction is $1.5$.

For the other reactions:
$\text{H}_{2(g)} + \text{I}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow 2\text{HI}_{(g)}$ follows second-order kinetics.
$2\text{H}_2\text{O}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}_{(\ell)} + \text{O}_{2(g)}$ follows first-order kinetics.
$2\text{NO}_{(g)} + 2\text{H}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow \text{N}_{2(g)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}_{(\ell)}$ follows third-order kinetics.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}_{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{CH}_{4(g)} + \text{CO}_{(g)}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For the reaction $2\text{NOBr}_{(g)} \longrightarrow 2\text{NO}_{(g)} + \text{Br}_{2(g)}$, rate law is $r = k[\text{NOBr}]^2$. Rate constant is $1.62\ \text{M s}^{-1}$ and concentration of NOBr is $5 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{M}$,
What is rate of reaction?
questions.solution:
Given rate law is $r = k[\text{NOBr}]^2$

Substituting the given values:

$r = 1.62 \times (5 \times 10^{-3})^2$

$r = 1.62 \times 25 \times 10^{-6}$

$r = 40.5 \times 10^{-6}$

$r = 4.05 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{M s}^{-1}$

Answer: $4.05 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{M s}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a first order reaction 20 millimole of reactant is lowered to 10 millimole in $0.3010$ minute. Find rate constant of the reaction?
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by the expression:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \left( \dfrac{a}{a - x} \right)$

Given:
Initial amount, $a = 20$ millimole
Amount after time $t$, $a - x = 10$ millimole
Time, $t = 0.3010$ minute

Substituting the given values into the equation:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{0.3010} \log \left( \dfrac{20}{10} \right)$

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{0.3010} \log 2$

Using the standard value $\log 2 = 0.3010$:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{0.3010} \times 0.3010$

$k = 2.303\ \text{minute}^{-1}$

Answer: $2.303\ \text{minute}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which medicinal property is exhibited by methylsalicylate?
questions.solution:
Methyl salicylate, commonly known as oil of wintergreen, is widely used in medicine as an analgesic.

It is applied topically in the form of ointments and liniments to relieve muscle and joint pain.

Therefore, it exhibits analgesic properties.

Answer: Analgesic

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find EAN of Fe in $\text{Fe(CO)}_5$
questions.solution:
The Effective Atomic Number (EAN) is calculated using the formula:

$\text{EAN} = Z - \text{Oxidation State} + 2 \times \text{Coordination Number}$

For $\text{Fe(CO)}_5$:

Atomic number of Fe ($Z$) = $26$

Oxidation state of Fe = $0$ (since CO is a neutral ligand)

Coordination number = $5$

$\text{EAN} = 26 - 0 + 2 \times 5$

$\text{EAN} = 26 + 10 = 36$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a ligand with highest field strength among the following.
questions.solution:
According to the spectrochemical series, the arrangement of ligands in the increasing order of their crystal field splitting energy (CFSE) values is:

$I^- \lt Br^- \lt SCN^- \lt Cl^- \lt S^{2-} \lt F^- \lt OH^- \lt C_2O_4^{2-} \lt H_2O \lt NCS^- \lt edta^{4-} \lt NH_3 \lt en \lt CN^- \lt CO$

From the given options, the order of field strength is $S^{2-} \lt H_2O \lt NCS^- \lt NH_3$.

Thus, $\text{NH}_3$ has the highest field strength.

Answer: $\text{NH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the total number of transition series of d-block elements?
questions.solution:
The d-block elements are distributed into four transition series based on the filling of d-orbitals:

First transition series ($3d$ series): Sc ($Z=21$) to Zn ($Z=30$)

Second transition series ($4d$ series): Y ($Z=39$) to Cd ($Z=48$)

Third transition series ($5d$ series): La ($Z=57$), Hf ($Z=72$) to Hg ($Z=80$)

Fourth transition series ($6d$ series): Ac ($Z=89$), Rf ($Z=104$) to Cn ($Z=112$)

Therefore, there are a total of $4$ transition series of d-block elements.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which actinoid from following has smallest ionic size in $+3$ state?
questions.solution:
In the actinoid series, as the atomic number increases from Actinium (Ac) to Lawrencium (Lr), there is a gradual decrease in the size of atoms or $M^{3+}$ ions. This phenomenon is known as actinoid contraction, which is due to the poor shielding effect of the $5f$ electrons.

The given elements belong to the actinoid series with the following atomic numbers:
Pa ($Z = 91$)
Cm ($Z = 96$)
Fm ($Z = 100$)
Lr ($Z = 103$)

Since Lawrencium (Lr) has the highest atomic number among the given options, it experiences the maximum actinoid contraction. Therefore, $Lr^{3+}$ has the smallest ionic size.

Answer: Lr

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following net cell reactions occurs in a galvanic cell containing cadmium electrode and standard hydrogen electrode?
$\text{E}^\circ_{(\text{Cd}^{2+}_{(aq)}|\text{Cd}_{(s)})} = -0.403\ \text{V}$.
questions.solution:
Given $E^\circ_{\text{Cd}^{2+}|\text{Cd}} = -0.403\ \text{V}$ and $E^\circ_{\text{H}^+|\text{H}_2} = 0.00\ \text{V}$.

Since the standard reduction potential of cadmium is lower than that of hydrogen, cadmium has a higher tendency to get oxidized. Therefore, cadmium will act as the anode (oxidation) and the standard hydrogen electrode will act as the cathode (reduction).

At anode: $\text{Cd}_{(s)} \longrightarrow \text{Cd}^{2+}_{(aq)} + 2\text{e}^-$

At cathode: $2\text{H}^+_{(aq)} + 2\text{e}^- \longrightarrow \text{H}_{2(g)}$

Adding the two half-cell reactions, the net cell reaction is:

$\text{Cd}_{(s)} + 2\text{H}^+_{(aq)} \longrightarrow \text{Cd}^{2+}_{(aq)} + \text{H}_{2(g)}$

Answer: $\text{Cd}_{(s)} + 2\text{H}^+_{(aq)} \longrightarrow \text{Cd}^{2+}_{(aq)} + \text{H}_{2(g)}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a certain redox reaction in galvanic cell $\text{X}_{(s)} + \text{Y}^{2+}_{(aq)} \longrightarrow \text{X}^{2+}_{(aq)} + \text{Y}_{(s)}$, $\text{E}^\circ$ cell is $0.0296\ \text{V}$ at $298\ \text{K}$. What is equilibrium constant of reaction?
questions.solution:
The relation between standard cell potential and equilibrium constant at $298\ \text{K}$ is given by:

$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = \dfrac{0.0591}{n} \log K_c$

For the given reaction, the number of electrons transferred is $n = 2$.

Substituting the given values:

$0.0296 = \dfrac{0.0591}{2} \log K_c$

$0.0296 \approx 0.02955 \log K_c$

$\log K_c = \dfrac{0.0296}{0.02955} \approx 1$

$K_c = 10^1 = 10$

Answer: $10$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the of number of chiral carbon atoms present in 2-Bromo-3,4,5-trimethylhexane ?
questions.solution:
The structure of 2-Bromo-3,4,5-trimethylhexane is:

$CH_3 - CH(Br) - CH(CH_3) - CH(CH_3) - CH(CH_3) - CH_3$

Let us examine each carbon atom in the principal chain for chirality (a chiral carbon must be attached to four different groups):

C1: Attached to three identical hydrogen atoms \Rightarrow Achiral.

C2: Attached to $-H$, $-Br$, $-CH_3$, and $-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)_2$. All four groups are different \Rightarrow Chiral.

C3: Attached to $-H$, $-CH_3$, $-CH(Br)CH_3$, and $-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)_2$. All four groups are different \Rightarrow Chiral.

C4: Attached to $-H$, $-CH_3$, $-CH(CH_3)CH(Br)CH_3$, and $-CH(CH_3)_2$. All four groups are different \Rightarrow Chiral.

C5: Attached to $-H$, a methyl group ($-CH_3$), C6 (which is also a $-CH_3$ group), and $-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH(Br)CH_3$. Since it is attached to two identical methyl groups, it is \Rightarrow Achiral.

C6: Attached to three identical hydrogen atoms \Rightarrow Achiral.

The chiral carbon atoms are C2, C3, and C4. Therefore, there are 3 chiral carbon atoms in the molecule.

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the name of second higher homologue of formic acid?
questions.solution:
Formic acid is the first member of the carboxylic acid homologous series with the IUPAC name methanoic acid ($HCOOH$).

The first higher homologue is obtained by adding one $-CH_2-$ group, which gives ethanoic acid ($CH_3COOH$).

The second higher homologue is obtained by adding another $-CH_2-$ group, which gives propanoic acid ($CH_3CH_2COOH$).

Answer: Propanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The reaction of aryl halide with sodium metal in dry ether to give biphenyl is known as
questions.solution:
The reaction of an aryl halide with sodium metal in the presence of dry ether to form biphenyl is known as the Fittig reaction.

$2\text{Ar-X} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{Ar-Ar} + 2\text{NaX}$

The Wurtz reaction involves two alkyl halides to form an alkane, while the Wurtz-Fittig reaction involves one alkyl halide and one aryl halide to form an alkylarene. The Swarts reaction is used for the synthesis of alkyl fluorides.

Answer: Fittig reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkyl chlorides on Wurtz reaction gives 2, 2, 5, 5- tetramethylhexane ?
questions.solution:
Wurtz reaction involves the coupling of two alkyl halide molecules in the presence of sodium and dry ether to form a symmetrical alkane.

$2\text{R-Cl} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{R-R} + 2\text{NaCl}$

The given product is 2,2,5,5-tetramethylhexane. Its structure is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_3$.

Cleaving the molecule symmetrically at the central $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond gives two identical alkyl groups, which are neopentyl groups, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-$.

Therefore, the required alkyl chloride is neopentyl chloride, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the conjugate bases of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ respectively from following.
questions.solution:
The conjugate base of a Bronsted acid is formed by the removal of one proton ($H^+$) from it.

For $H_3PO_3$, the removal of one $H^+$ yields its conjugate base:

$H_3PO_3 \rightarrow H^+ + H_2PO_3^-$

For $H_2SO_4$, the removal of one $H^+$ yields its conjugate base:

$H_2SO_4 \rightarrow H^+ + HSO_4^-$

Therefore, the conjugate bases of $H_3PO_3$ and $H_2SO_4$ are $H_2PO_3^-$ and $HSO_4^-$ respectively.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the molarity of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution having $\text{pH} = 4$ ?
questions.solution:
Given $\text{pH} = 4$

$[\text{H}^+] = 10^{-4}\ \text{M}$

$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is a strong diprotic acid and dissociates completely in dilute solutions:

$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow 2\text{H}^+ + \text{SO}_4^{2-}$

Therefore, $[\text{H}^+] = 2 \times [\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4]$

$[\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4] = \dfrac{[\text{H}^+]}{2} = \dfrac{10^{-4}}{2} = 5 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{M}$

Answer: $5 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{M}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The solubility of a sparingly soluble a salt $\text{AB}_2$ is $1 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{mol/dm}^3$. Calculate its solubility product?
questions.solution:
The dissociation of the salt $AB_2$ is given by:

$AB_2 \rightleftharpoons A^{2+} + 2B^-$

Let the solubility of the salt be $S$. The equilibrium concentrations are:

$[A^{2+}] = S$

$[B^-] = 2S$

The solubility product $K_{sp}$ is:

$K_{sp} = [A^{2+}][B^-]^2$

$K_{sp} = (S)(2S)^2 = 4S^3$

Given $S = 1 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{mol/dm}^3$, substituting this value:

$K_{sp} = 4(1 \times 10^{-6})^3$

$K_{sp} = 4 \times 10^{-18}$

Answer: $4 \times 10^{-18}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is Lewis acid?
questions.solution:
A Lewis acid is a chemical species that can accept a pair of electrons.

In $\text{BeCl}_2$, the central beryllium atom forms two single covalent bonds with two chlorine atoms. The valence shell of beryllium in this molecule contains only $4$ electrons, which means its octet is incomplete.

Due to this electron deficiency, $\text{BeCl}_2$ has a strong tendency to accept electron pairs from other species (Lewis bases) to complete its octet. For example, in the solid state, it forms a polymeric chain structure through coordinate bonding where chlorine atoms donate electron pairs to adjacent beryllium atoms.

The other given compounds ($\text{BaCl}_2$, $\text{KCl}$, $\text{LiCl}$) are predominantly ionic, and their respective cations have stable noble gas (or duplet) configurations, so they do not act as Lewis acids.

Answer: $\text{BeCl}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the formula of Tin (IV) oxide?
questions.solution:
The oxidation state of Tin (Sn) in Tin (IV) oxide is $+4$.

The oxidation state of Oxygen (O) in an oxide ion is $-2$.

To form a neutral compound, the total positive charge must balance the total negative charge. Two oxide ions are required to balance one Tin (IV) ion.

Using the criss-cross method, the formula is initially $\text{Sn}_2\text{O}_4$, which simplifies to the empirical formula $\text{SnO}_2$.

Answer: $\text{SnO}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is NOT obtained by addition polymerisation method?
questions.solution:
Teflon is an addition polymer of tetrafluoroethene.

Polyacrylonitrile is an addition polymer of acrylonitrile.

LDP (Low-density polyethylene) is an addition polymer of ethene.

PHBV (Poly $\beta$-hydroxybutyrate-co-$\beta$-hydroxyvalerate) is a condensation polymer of 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid.

Answer: PHBV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens in the oxidation number of Mn during working of dry cell.
questions.solution:
In a dry cell, the reaction at the cathode involves the reduction of manganese dioxide ($MnO_2$).

The cathode reaction is:
$MnO_2 + NH_4^+ + e^- \rightarrow MnO(OH) + NH_3$

The oxidation state of Mn in $MnO_2$ is $+4$.
The oxidation state of Mn in $MnO(OH)$ is $+3$.

The oxidation number of Mn changes from $+4$ to $+3$. Thus, the oxidation number of Mn decreases by $1$.

Answer: decreases by 1

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the total number of Bravais lattices in orthorhombic crystal system?
questions.solution:
The orthorhombic crystal system has $4$ Bravais lattices.

These are:
1. Primitive (P)
2. Body-centered (I)
3. Face-centered (F)
4. Base-centered or End-centered (C)

Therefore, the total number of Bravais lattices in the orthorhombic crystal system is $4$.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the void volume in fcc unit cell if total volume of a unit cell is $6.4 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3$ ?
questions.solution:
The packing efficiency of a face-centered cubic (fcc) unit cell is $74\%$.

The percentage of void space in the fcc unit cell is $100\% - 74\% = 26\%$.

Given the total volume of the unit cell is $V = 6.4 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3$.

Void volume $= 0.26 \times V$

Void volume $= 0.26 \times 6.4 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3 = 1.664 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3$

Answer: $1.664 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the number of atoms present in $1\ \text{g}$ metal that forms simple unit cell structure if product of density and volume of unit cell is $66.5 \times 10^{-24}\ \text{g}$
questions.solution:
For a simple cubic unit cell, the number of atoms per unit cell is $Z = 1$.

The mass of one unit cell is equal to the product of its density and volume.

Mass of one unit cell = $\rho \times V = 66.5 \times 10^{-24} \text{ g}$.

Since there is $1$ atom per unit cell, the mass of one atom is $66.5 \times 10^{-24} \text{ g}$.

The number of atoms in $1 \text{ g}$ of the metal is given by:

Number of atoms = $\dfrac{\text{Total mass}}{\text{Mass of one atom}}$

Number of atoms = $\dfrac{1}{66.5 \times 10^{-24}}$

Number of atoms = $0.015037 \times 10^{24}$

Number of atoms $\approx 1.504 \times 10^{22}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify correct statements from following regarding $0.2\ \text{M}$ urea and $0.2\ \text{M}$ sucrose solutions.
options: The urea solution is hypertonic to sucrose solution.
The osmotic pressure of urea solution is higher than that of sucrose solution.
These solutions exhibit same osmotic pressure.
The sucrose solution is hypotonic to urea solution.
questions.solution:
Osmotic pressure is given by $\pi = iCRT$.

For urea, $i = 1$ and $C = 0.2\ \text{M}$.

For sucrose, $i = 1$ and $C = 0.2\ \text{M}$.

Since both solutions have the same concentration and the same van 't Hoff factor, their osmotic pressures are equal at a given temperature.

Therefore, these solutions exhibit the same osmotic pressure and are isotonic to each other.

Answer: These solutions exhibit same osmotic pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the molality of solution of nonvolatile solute if boiling point of solution, molal elevation constant for solvent are $319.8\ \text{K}$ and $2.5\ \text{K kg mol}^{-1}$ respectively [Boiling point of solvent = $319.5\ \text{K}$]
questions.solution:
Elevation in boiling point is given by $\Delta T_b = T_b - T_b^\circ$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta T_b = 319.8 - 319.5 = 0.3\ \text{K}$

The relation between elevation in boiling point and molality is $\Delta T_b = K_b \times m$

Rearranging for molality $m$:

$m = \dfrac{\Delta T_b}{K_b}$

$m = \dfrac{0.3}{2.5} = 0.12\ \text{mol kg}^{-1}$

Answer: $0.12\ \text{mol kg}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $40$ gram nonelectrolyte solute having molar mass $180\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$ dissolved in water has osmotic pressure $2\ \text{atm}$ at $300\ \text{K}$. Calculate the volume of solution. ($\text{R} = 0.0821\ \text{atm mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Using the formula for osmotic pressure:

$\pi = \dfrac{n}{V}RT$

Rearranging for volume $V$:

$V = \dfrac{nRT}{\pi}$

Number of moles of solute $n = \dfrac{40}{180} = \dfrac{2}{9}\ \text{mol}$

Substituting the given values:

$V = \dfrac{\dfrac{2}{9} \times 0.0821 \times 300}{2}$

$V = \dfrac{24.63}{9}$

$V = 2.736\ \text{L}$

Since $1\ \text{L} = 1\ \text{dm}^3$, the volume of the solution is $2.74\ \text{dm}^3$.

Answer: $2.74\ \text{dm}^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many moles of potassium chlorate are heated to produce $22.4\ \text{lit}$ of oxygen at STP ?
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the thermal decomposition of potassium chlorate is:

$2KClO_3 \rightarrow 2KCl + 3O_2$

At STP, $22.4\ \text{lit}$ of oxygen gas corresponds to $1\ \text{mole}$ of $O_2$.

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $3\ \text{moles}$ of $O_2$ are produced by heating $2\ \text{moles}$ of $KClO_3$.

Therefore, the number of moles of $KClO_3$ required to produce $1\ \text{mole}$ of $O_2$ is $\dfrac{2}{3}\ \text{mole}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{3}\ \text{mole}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What ratio by mass of 'Ne' and $\text{CH}_4$ should be mixed so that partial pressure exerted by each gas is same?
questions.solution:
Let the mass of Ne be $w_1$ and the mass of $\text{CH}_4$ be $w_2$.

Molar mass of Ne $= 20 \text{ g/mol}$
Molar mass of $\text{CH}_4 = 16 \text{ g/mol}$

Number of moles of Ne, $n_{\text{Ne}} = \dfrac{w_1}{20}$
Number of moles of $\text{CH}_4$, $n_{\text{CH}_4} = \dfrac{w_2}{16}$

According to Dalton's law of partial pressures, the partial pressure of a gas in a mixture is directly proportional to its number of moles. Since the partial pressures of both gases are equal, their number of moles must be equal.

$n_{\text{Ne}} = n_{\text{CH}_4}$

$\dfrac{w_1}{20} = \dfrac{w_2}{16}$

$\dfrac{w_1}{w_2} = \dfrac{20}{16} = \dfrac{5}{4}$

The required ratio by mass is $5:4$.

Answer: $5:4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following colours of visible light has lowest energy?
questions.solution:
The energy of a photon is given by the relation $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$.

This shows that energy is inversely proportional to the wavelength of light.

In the visible spectrum (VIBGYOR), red light has the maximum wavelength.

Therefore, red light has the lowest energy.

Answer: Red

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following anions has greater power for coagulation of positive sol?
questions.solution:
According to the Hardy-Schulze rule, the coagulating power of an ion is directly proportional to the magnitude of its charge (valency). For the coagulation of a positive sol, an anion is required.

The given anions and their charge magnitudes are:
$\text{Cl}^-$ : $1$
$\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ : $2$
$\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ (given as $\text{PO}_4^{2-}$ in options) : $3$
$[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ : $4$

Since $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ has the highest negative charge, it possesses the maximum coagulating power among the given options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is correct expression of first law of thermodynamics for isothermal process?
questions.solution:
According to the first law of thermodynamics, the change in internal energy is given by $\Delta U = Q + W$.

For an isothermal process, the temperature of the system remains constant, so $\Delta T = 0$.

Since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, the change in internal energy is zero, $\Delta U = 0$.

Substituting $\Delta U = 0$ into the first law equation gives:

$0 = Q + W$

$W = -Q$

Answer: $\text{W} = -\text{Q}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a certain reaction, $\Delta\text{H}^\circ = 40\ \text{kJ}$ and $\Delta\text{S}^\circ = 80\ \text{JK}^{-1}$. Find the temperature so that $\Delta\text{G}^\circ = 0$
questions.solution:
Using the Gibbs free energy equation:

$\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ$

For $\Delta G^\circ = 0$, we get:

$T = \dfrac{\Delta H^\circ}{\Delta S^\circ}$

Given $\Delta H^\circ = 40\ \text{kJ} = 40000\ \text{J}$ and $\Delta S^\circ = 80\ \text{J K}^{-1}$.

Substituting the values:

$T = \dfrac{40000}{80} = 500\ \text{K}$

Answer: $500\ \text{K}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate $\Delta\text{H}$ for the following reaction at $300\ \text{K}$
$2\text{C}_{(s)} + 3\text{H}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_{6(g)}$ if $\Delta\text{U}$ for the reaction is $-80\ \text{kJ}$ ($\text{R} = 8.314\ \text{JK}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $2\text{C}_{(s)} + 3\text{H}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_{6(g)}$

Change in number of gaseous moles, $\Delta n_g = n_{p(g)} - n_{r(g)} = 1 - 3 = -2$

Given $\Delta\text{U} = -80\ \text{kJ}$

$T = 300\ \text{K}$

$R = 8.314\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1} = 8.314 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{kJ K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$

Using the relation $\Delta\text{H} = \Delta\text{U} + \Delta n_g RT$

$\Delta\text{H} = -80 + (-2) \times 8.314 \times 10^{-3} \times 300$

$\Delta\text{H} = -80 - 4.9884$

$\Delta\text{H} = -84.9884\ \text{kJ} \approx -85.00\ \text{kJ}$

Answer: $-85.00\ \text{kJ}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the side of an equilateral triangle increases at the rate of $\sqrt{3}\ \text{cm/sec}$, then the rate of change of increase of its area when the side is $12\ \text{cm}$ is ____
questions.solution:
Let the side of the equilateral triangle be $a$ and its area be $A$.

Given $\dfrac{da}{dt} = \sqrt{3}\ \text{cm/sec}$ and $a = 12\ \text{cm}$.

The area of an equilateral triangle is given by $A = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2$.

Differentiating with respect to time $t$:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 2a \times \dfrac{da}{dt}$

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}a \dfrac{da}{dt}$

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 12 \times \sqrt{3}$

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = 6 \times 3 = 18\ \text{cm}^2/\text{sec}$

Answer: $18\ \text{cm}^2/\text{sec}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the tangent to the curve $xy + ax + by = 0$ at $(1,1)$ makes an angle of $\tan^{-1}2$ with positive direction of the $x$-axis, then the value of $\dfrac{ab}{a+b}$ is...
questions.solution:
Since the point $(1,1)$ lies on the curve $xy + ax + by = 0$, substituting $x=1$ and $y=1$ gives:

$1 + a + b = 0 \Rightarrow a + b = -1$

Differentiating the equation of the curve with respect to $x$, we get:

$y + x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + a + b\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{y+a}{x+b}$

The slope of the tangent at $(1,1)$ is given as $\tan(\tan^{-1}2) = 2$.

$\left. \dfrac{dy}{dx} \right|_{(1,1)} = -\dfrac{1+a}{1+b} = 2$

$-1 - a = 2 + 2b \Rightarrow a + 2b = -3$

Solving $a + b = -1$ and $a + 2b = -3$, we get:

$b = -2$ and $a = 1$

The value of $\dfrac{ab}{a+b}$ is:

$\dfrac{(1)(-2)}{-1} = 2$

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the line $x + By + C = 0$ is the normal to the curve given by $x = a\sin^3 t$, $y = b\cos^3 t$, (where $a, b \neq 0$) at a point $t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, then $B - C = $
questions.solution:
Given the parametric equations of the curve:

$x = a\sin^3 t$

$y = b\cos^3 t$

At $t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, the coordinates of the point on the curve are:

$x = a\sin^3\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = a(1)^3 = a$

$y = b\cos^3\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = b(0)^3 = 0$

So, the point is $(a, 0)$.

Differentiating $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t$:

$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 3a\sin^2 t \cos t$

$\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -3b\cos^2 t \sin t$

The slope of the tangent to the curve is:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\dfrac{dy}{dt}}{\dfrac{dx}{dt}} = \dfrac{-3b\cos^2 t \sin t}{3a\sin^2 t \cos t} = -\dfrac{b}{a}\cot t$

At $t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, the slope of the tangent is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{b}{a}\cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0$.

Since the tangent is horizontal, the normal to the curve is vertical (parallel to the y-axis).

The equation of the vertical normal passing through $(a, 0)$ is:

$x = a \Rightarrow x + 0 \cdot y - a = 0$

Comparing this with the given equation of the normal $x + By + C = 0$, we get:

$B = 0$

$C = -a$

Therefore, the value of $B - C$ is:

$B - C = 0 - (-a) = a$

Answer: $a$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area (in square units) bounded by the line $y = x$, the X-axis and the lines $x = -2$ and $x = 4$ is...
questions.solution:
The required area is given by the integral of $|y|$ with respect to $x$ from $x = -2$ to $x = 4$.

$A = \int_{-2}^{4} |x| dx$

$A = \int_{-2}^{0} (-x) dx + \int_{0}^{4} x dx$

$A = \left[ -\dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_{-2}^{0} + \left[ \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{4}$

$A = \left(0 - \left(-\dfrac{4}{2}\right)\right) + \left(\dfrac{16}{2} - 0\right)$

$A = 2 + 8 = 10$

Answer: $10$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The tangent to the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 10$ at the point $(3,1)$ touches the circle $x^2 + y^2 - 2\sqrt{10}\,x - 20y + k = 0$, then the value of $k$ is...
questions.solution:
The equation of the tangent to the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 10$ at the point $(3,1)$ is given by $T = 0$:

$3x + y = 10 \Rightarrow 3x + y - 10 = 0$

The equation of the second circle is $x^2 + y^2 - 2\sqrt{10}x - 20y + k = 0$.

The center of this circle is $(\sqrt{10}, 10)$ and its radius is $r = \sqrt{(\sqrt{10})^2 + (10)^2 - k} = \sqrt{110 - k}$.

Since the line $3x + y - 10 = 0$ touches the second circle, the perpendicular distance from the center to the line must be equal to the radius of the circle.

The perpendicular distance $d$ is:

$d = \dfrac{|3(\sqrt{10}) + 10 - 10|}{\sqrt{3^2 + 1^2}} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{10}} = 3$

Equating the distance to the radius:

$\sqrt{110 - k} = 3$

Squaring both sides:

$110 - k = 9$

$k = 101$

Answer: $101$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region (in sq. unit) bounded by x-axis, the tangent and normal to the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 4$, drawn at a point $(1, \sqrt{3})$ is
questions.solution:
Equation of the circle is $x^2 + y^2 = 4$.

Equation of the tangent at the point $(1, \sqrt{3})$ is given by $xx_1 + yy_1 = r^2$, which is $x + \sqrt{3}y = 4$.

Equation of the normal at $(1, \sqrt{3})$ passes through the origin $(0,0)$, so its equation is $y = \sqrt{3}x$.

The region bounded by the tangent, normal, and the x-axis ($y=0$) forms a triangle. We find its vertices by solving the equations of the lines pairwise.

Intersection of the normal and the x-axis is $(0, 0)$.

Intersection of the tangent and the x-axis is obtained by putting $y=0$ in $x + \sqrt{3}y = 4$, which gives $x=4$. The point is $(4, 0)$.

Intersection of the tangent and the normal is the point of contact $(1, \sqrt{3})$.

The base of the triangle lies on the x-axis with length $4 - 0 = 4$.

The height of the triangle is the y-coordinate of the point $(1, \sqrt{3})$, which is $\sqrt{3}$.

Area of the triangle $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times \sqrt{3} = 2\sqrt{3}$ sq. units.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $\left(\dfrac{-1+i\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^{18} + \left(\dfrac{-1-i\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^{18}$ is
questions.solution:
Let $\omega = \dfrac{-1+i\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\omega^2 = \dfrac{-1-i\sqrt{3}}{2}$ be the complex cube roots of unity.

The given expression can be written as $\omega^{18} + (\omega^2)^{18}$.

Since $\omega^3 = 1$, we have $\omega^{18} = (\omega^3)^6 = 1^6 = 1$.

Similarly, $(\omega^2)^{18} = \omega^{36} = (\omega^3)^{12} = 1^{12} = 1$.

Therefore, the value of the expression is $1 + 1 = 2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The number of point / points where the function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x^2-5|x|+6}$ is discontinuous is......
questions.solution:
The function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x^2-5|x|+6}$ is discontinuous at the points where its denominator is zero.

$x^2 - 5|x| + 6 = 0$

Since $x^2 = |x|^2$, the equation can be written as:

$|x|^2 - 5|x| + 6 = 0$

$(|x| - 2)(|x| - 3) = 0$

$|x| = 2 \Rightarrow x = \pm 2$

$|x| = 3 \Rightarrow x = \pm 3$

The points of discontinuity are $x = -3, -2, 2, 3$.

The number of points where the function is discontinuous is $4$.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $[\cdot]$ denotes the greatest integer function, then $\int_0^{\pi/3}[\tan x]\,dx = $
questions.solution:
The given integral is $I = \int_0^{\pi/3} [\tan x] \, dx$.

In the interval $[0, \pi/3]$, the function $\tan x$ is strictly increasing.

For $0 \le x \lt \pi/4$, $0 \le \tan x \lt 1 \Rightarrow [\tan x] = 0$.

For $\pi/4 \le x \le \pi/3$, $1 \le \tan x \le \sqrt{3} \lt 2 \Rightarrow [\tan x] = 1$.

Splitting the integral at $x = \pi/4$, we get:

$I = \int_0^{\pi/4} 0 \, dx + \int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/3} 1 \, dx$

$I = 0 + [x]_{\pi/4}^{\pi/3}$

$I = \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{12}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{12}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of the definite integral $\int_0^{\log_e 5}\dfrac{e^x\sqrt{e^x-1}}{e^x+3}\,dx$ is equal to...
questions.solution:
Let $e^x - 1 = t^2$, which gives $e^x dx = 2t dt$.

When $x = 0$, $t = 0$.

When $x = \log_e 5$, $t = 2$.

The integral becomes:

$I = \int_0^2 \dfrac{t}{t^2 + 1 + 3} (2t dt) = \int_0^2 \dfrac{2t^2}{t^2 + 4} dt$

$I = 2 \int_0^2 \dfrac{t^2 + 4 - 4}{t^2 + 4} dt$

$I = 2 \int_0^2 \left( 1 - \dfrac{4}{t^2 + 4} \right) dt$

$I = 2 \left[ t - 4 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \tan^{-1} \left( \dfrac{t}{2} \right) \right]_0^2$

$I = 2 \left[ 2 - 2 \tan^{-1}(1) \right]$

$I = 2 \left( 2 - 2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{4} \right)$

$I = 4 - \pi$

Answer: $4 - \pi$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation $x\sin x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + (x\cos x + \sin x)y = \sin x$ is
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is $x\sin x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + (x\cos x + \sin x)y = \sin x$

Observing the left hand side, it can be rewritten using the product rule of differentiation:

$x\sin x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\dfrac{d}{dx}(x\sin x) = \sin x$

$\dfrac{d}{dx}(xy\sin x) = \sin x$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$:

$\int \dfrac{d}{dx}(xy\sin x) dx = \int \sin x dx$

$xy\sin x = -\cos x + c$

$xy\sin x + \cos x = c$

Answer: $xy\sin x + \cos x = c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A body cools from $100^\circ\text{C}$ to $60^\circ\text{C}$ in 20 minutes, the temperature of the surroundings being $20^\circ\text{C}$. The total time taken (in minutes) for the body to cool down to $40^\circ\text{C}$ is ...
questions.solution:
Using Newton's law of cooling:

$\ln\left(\dfrac{T_1 - T_s}{T_2 - T_s}\right) = kt$

For the first interval, the body cools from $100^\circ\text{C}$ to $60^\circ\text{C}$ in $20$ minutes with $T_s = 20^\circ\text{C}$:

$\ln\left(\dfrac{100 - 20}{60 - 20}\right) = k(20)$

$\ln\left(\dfrac{80}{40}\right) = 20k$

$\ln(2) = 20k$

For the total time $t$ to cool from $100^\circ\text{C}$ to $40^\circ\text{C}$:

$\ln\left(\dfrac{100 - 20}{40 - 20}\right) = kt$

$\ln\left(\dfrac{80}{20}\right) = kt$

$\ln(4) = kt$

$2\ln(2) = kt$

Substituting $20k$ for $\ln(2)$:

$2(20k) = kt$

$t = 40$ minutes

Answer: $40$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the curve whose slope is $\dfrac{y-1}{x^2+x}$ and which passes through the point $(1, 0)$ is
questions.solution:
The slope of the curve is given by $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y-1}{x^2+x}$

Separating the variables, we get:

$\dfrac{dy}{y-1} = \dfrac{dx}{x(x+1)}$

Integrating both sides:

$\int \dfrac{dy}{y-1} = \int \left( \dfrac{1}{x} - \dfrac{1}{x+1} \right) dx$

$\ln|y-1| = \ln|x| - \ln|x+1| + \ln|C|$

$\ln|y-1| = \ln\left|\dfrac{Cx}{x+1}\right|$

$y-1 = \dfrac{Cx}{x+1}$

Since the curve passes through the point $(1, 0)$, we substitute $x = 1$ and $y = 0$:

$0 - 1 = \dfrac{C(1)}{1+1}$

$-1 = \dfrac{C}{2} \Rightarrow C = -2$

Substituting $C = -2$ back into the equation:

$y-1 = \dfrac{-2x}{x+1}$

$(y-1)(x+1) = -2x$

$xy + y - x - 1 = -2x$

$xy + x + y - 1 = 0$

Answer: $xy + x + y - 1 = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $g(x) = (x^2 + 2x + 1)\cdot f(x)$ such that $f(0) = 5$ and $\lim\limits_{x \to 0}\dfrac{f(x)-5}{x} = 4$ then $g'(0) = $
questions.solution:
Given $g(x) = (x^2 + 2x + 1) f(x)$

Differentiating with respect to $x$ using the product rule:

$g'(x) = (2x + 2) f(x) + (x^2 + 2x + 1) f'(x)$

Substituting $x = 0$:

$g'(0) = 2 f(0) + f'(0)$

From the given limit, $\lim\limits_{x \to 0}\dfrac{f(x)-5}{x} = 4$, which represents the derivative of $f(x)$ at $x = 0$.

Thus, $f'(0) = 4$.

Also given $f(0) = 5$.

Substituting these values:

$g'(0) = 2(5) + 4 = 14$

Answer: $14$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x\,e^{xy} = y + \sin^2 x$, then the value of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $x = 0$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given equation is $x e^{xy} = y + \sin^2 x$.

Substituting $x = 0$ to find the corresponding value of $y$:

$0 \cdot e^0 = y + \sin^2 0 \Rightarrow y = 0$

Differentiating the given equation with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{d}{dx}(x e^{xy}) = \dfrac{d}{dx}(y + \sin^2 x)$

$e^{xy} + x e^{xy} \left(y + x \dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = \dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2 \sin x \cos x$

Substituting $x = 0$ and $y = 0$ into the differentiated equation:

$e^0 + 0 \cdot e^0 \left(0 + 0 \cdot \dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = \dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2 \sin 0 \cos 0$

$1 + 0 = \dfrac{dy}{dx} + 0$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1$

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the eccentricity of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1, (a  \gt  b)$ is $\dfrac{2}{3}$ and its focal chord is $3x + 2y - 6 = 0$, then the value of $a^2 + b^2$ is...
questions.solution:
The equation of the given ellipse is $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$ with $a \gt b$.

The foci of the ellipse are $(\pm ae, 0)$.

Since the line $3x + 2y - 6 = 0$ is a focal chord, it must pass through one of the foci. Substituting $y = 0$ in the equation of the line:

$3x + 0 - 6 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2$

Thus, the focus is $(2, 0)$, which gives $ae = 2$.

Given the eccentricity $e = \dfrac{2}{3}$, substituting this value yields:

$a \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = 2 \Rightarrow a = 3$

Squaring both sides, $a^2 = 9$.

For an ellipse, the relation between $a, b,$ and $e$ is given by $b^2 = a^2(1 - e^2)$.

Substituting the values of $a^2$ and $e$:

$b^2 = 9 \left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right) = 9 \left(\dfrac{5}{9}\right) = 5$

The value of $a^2 + b^2$ is:

$a^2 + b^2 = 9 + 5 = 14$

Answer: $14$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $f(x) = ax + b$ and $g(x) = cx + d$. The condition $f(g(x)) = g(f(x))$ holds for all $x$ if and only if ...
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = ax + b$ and $g(x) = cx + d$.

Substituting $g(x)$ into $f(x)$:

$f(g(x)) = a(cx + d) + b = acx + ad + b$

Substituting $f(x)$ into $g(x)$:

$g(f(x)) = c(ax + b) + d = acx + cb + d$

For $f(g(x)) = g(f(x))$ to hold for all $x$, the corresponding coefficients and constant terms must be equal:

$acx + ad + b = acx + cb + d$

$ad + b = cb + d$

Now, evaluating $f(d)$ and $g(b)$:

$f(d) = ad + b$

$g(b) = cb + d$

Therefore, the required condition is $f(d) = g(b)$.

Answer: $f(d) = g(b)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int\dfrac{(x+1)\,dx}{x(1+xe^x)} = \ldots\ldots$
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int\dfrac{x+1}{x(1+xe^x)} dx$

Multiplying the numerator and the denominator by $e^x$:

$I = \int\dfrac{(x+1)e^x}{xe^x(1+xe^x)} dx$

Let $xe^x = t$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$(1 \cdot e^x + x \cdot e^x) dx = dt$

$(x+1)e^x dx = dt$

Substituting these into the integral:

$I = \int\dfrac{dt}{t(1+t)}$

Using partial fractions:

$I = \int\left(\dfrac{1}{t} - \dfrac{1}{1+t}\right) dt$

$I = \log|t| - \log|1+t| + c$

$I = \log\left|\dfrac{t}{1+t}\right| + c$

Substituting $t = xe^x$ back into the expression:

$I = \log\left|\dfrac{xe^x}{1+xe^x}\right| + c$

Answer: $\log\left|\dfrac{xe^x}{1+xe^x}\right| + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $\int\dfrac{n\sqrt{\text{cosec}^2 x^n - 1}}{x^{(1-n)}}\,dx$ is ...
questions.solution:
Let the given integral be $I = \int \dfrac{n\sqrt{\text{cosec}^2 x^n - 1}}{x^{(1-n)}} \,dx$

Using the trigonometric identity $\text{cosec}^2 \theta - 1 = \cot^2 \theta$, the integral simplifies to:

$I = \int \dfrac{n \cot x^n}{x^{1-n}} \,dx$

$I = \int n x^{n-1} \cot x^n \,dx$

Let $x^n = t$, which gives $n x^{n-1} \,dx = dt$.

Substituting these into the integral, we get:

$I = \int \cot t \,dt$

$I = \log(\sin t) + c$

Substituting $t = x^n$ back into the expression:

$I = \log(\sin x^n) + c$

Answer: $\log(\sin x^n) + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int\sin(\log x)\,dx = $
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int \sin(\log x) \, dx$

Using integration by parts, taking $1$ as the second function:

$I = \sin(\log x) \int 1 \, dx - \int \left( \dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin(\log x)) \int 1 \, dx \right) dx$

$I = x \sin(\log x) - \int \cos(\log x) \cdot \dfrac{1}{x} \cdot x \, dx$

$I = x \sin(\log x) - \int \cos(\log x) \, dx$

Applying integration by parts again to the second integral:

$I = x \sin(\log x) - \left[ \cos(\log x) \int 1 \, dx - \int \left( \dfrac{d}{dx}(\cos(\log x)) \int 1 \, dx \right) dx \right]$

$I = x \sin(\log x) - \left[ x \cos(\log x) - \int \left( -\sin(\log x) \cdot \dfrac{1}{x} \cdot x \right) dx \right]$

$I = x \sin(\log x) - x \cos(\log x) - \int \sin(\log x) \, dx$

$I = x \sin(\log x) - x \cos(\log x) - I$

$2I = x [\sin(\log x) - \cos(\log x)]$

$I = \dfrac{x}{2} [\sin(\log x) - \cos(\log x)] + c$

Answer: $\dfrac{x}{2}[\sin(\log x) - \cos(\log x)] + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sum\limits_{n=1}^{2026}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{n^2+n+1}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x}\right)$, where $x \neq 0$, then $x = $
questions.solution:
The general term of the series is given by:

$T_n = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{n^2+n+1}\right)$

This can be rewritten as:

$T_n = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + n(n+1)}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{(n+1) - n}{1 + (n+1)n}\right)$

Using the formula $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x-y}{1+xy}\right) = \tan^{-1}(x) - \tan^{-1}(y)$, we get:

$T_n = \tan^{-1}(n+1) - \tan^{-1}(n)$

Summing from $n=1$ to $n=2026$, we obtain a telescoping series:

$\sum\limits_{n=1}^{2026} T_n = (\tan^{-1}(2) - \tan^{-1}(1)) + (\tan^{-1}(3) - \tan^{-1}(2)) + \dots + (\tan^{-1}(2027) - \tan^{-1}(2026))$

$\sum\limits_{n=1}^{2026} T_n = \tan^{-1}(2027) - \tan^{-1}(1)$

Applying the inverse tangent difference formula again:

$\tan^{-1}(2027) - \tan^{-1}(1) = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2027 - 1}{1 + 2027 \times 1}\right)$

$= \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2026}{2028}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1013}{1014}\right)$

We are given that this sum is equal to $\tan^{-1}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x}\right)$. Therefore:

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1013}{1014}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x}\right)$

Equating the arguments:

$\dfrac{1013}{1014} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{x}$

$\dfrac{1}{x} = 1 - \dfrac{1013}{1014} = \dfrac{1}{1014}$

$x = 1014$

Answer: $1014$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $0 \leq x \leq 1$ and $(\sin^{-1}x)^3 + (\cos^{-1}x)^3 = a\pi^3$ then
questions.solution:
Let $\sin^{-1}x = y$. Since $0 \leq x \leq 1$, we have $0 \leq y \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

We know that $\cos^{-1}x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{-1}x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - y$.

The given equation is:

$y^3 + \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - y\right)^3 = a\pi^3$

Using the identity $A^3 + B^3 = (A+B)(A^2 - AB + B^2)$, we get:

$y^3 + \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - y\right)^3 = \left(y + \dfrac{\pi}{2} - y\right) \left( y^2 - y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - y\right) + \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - y\right)^2 \right)$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{2} \left( y^2 - \dfrac{\pi}{2}y + y^2 + \dfrac{\pi^2}{4} - \pi y + y^2 \right)$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{2} \left( 3y^2 - \dfrac{3\pi}{2}y + \dfrac{\pi^2}{4} \right)$

$= \dfrac{3\pi}{2} \left( y^2 - \dfrac{\pi}{2}y + \dfrac{\pi^2}{12} \right)$

Completing the square for the quadratic in $y$:

$= \dfrac{3\pi}{2} \left( \left(y - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)^2 - \dfrac{\pi^2}{16} + \dfrac{\pi^2}{12} \right)$

$= \dfrac{3\pi}{2} \left( \left(y - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)^2 + \dfrac{\pi^2}{48} \right)$

$= \dfrac{3\pi}{2} \left(y - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)^2 + \dfrac{\pi^3}{32}$

Since $0 \leq y \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, the minimum value of this expression occurs at $y = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

Minimum value $= \dfrac{3\pi}{2} (0) + \dfrac{\pi^3}{32} = \dfrac{\pi^3}{32}$

The maximum value occurs at the endpoints $y = 0$ or $y = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Maximum value $= \dfrac{3\pi}{2} \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)^2 + \dfrac{\pi^3}{32} = \dfrac{3\pi^3}{32} + \dfrac{\pi^3}{32} = \dfrac{\pi^3}{8}$

Thus, the range of the expression is $\left[\dfrac{\pi^3}{32}, \dfrac{\pi^3}{8}\right]$.

Given that the expression equals $a\pi^3$, we have:

$\dfrac{\pi^3}{32} \leq a\pi^3 \leq \dfrac{\pi^3}{8}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{32} \leq a \leq \dfrac{1}{8}$

From the given options, the condition that is always satisfied is $a \geq \dfrac{1}{32}$.

Answer: $a \geq \dfrac{1}{32}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\log\left(\dfrac{e}{x^3}\right)}{\log ex^3}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\log(e^4x^3)}{\log\left(\dfrac{e}{x^{12}}\right)}\right)$, $x \in \left(e^{-\frac{1}{3}}, e^{\frac{1}{12}}\right)$ then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to...
questions.solution:
Given function is:

$y = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\log\left(\dfrac{e}{x^3}\right)}{\log(ex^3)}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\log(e^4x^3)}{\log\left(\dfrac{e}{x^{12}}\right)}\right)$

Using the properties of logarithms, we can simplify the arguments:

$\dfrac{\log\left(\dfrac{e}{x^3}\right)}{\log(ex^3)} = \dfrac{\log e - \log x^3}{\log e + \log x^3} = \dfrac{1 - 3\log x}{1 + 3\log x}$

$\dfrac{\log(e^4x^3)}{\log\left(\dfrac{e}{x^{12}}\right)} = \dfrac{\log e^4 + \log x^3}{\log e - \log x^{12}} = \dfrac{4 + 3\log x}{1 - 12\log x}$

Substituting these back into the expression for $y$:

$y = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - 3\log x}{1 + 1 \cdot 3\log x}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4 + 3\log x}{1 - 4 \cdot 3\log x}\right)$

We use the inverse trigonometric identities:
$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{a - b}{1 + ab}\right) = \tan^{-1}a - \tan^{-1}b$ (valid for $ab \gt -1$)
$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{a + b}{1 - ab}\right) = \tan^{-1}a + \tan^{-1}b$ (valid for $ab \lt 1$)

For the first term, $a = 1$ and $b = 3\log x$. Since $x \gt e^{-1/3}$, we have $3\log x \gt -1$, so $ab \gt -1$.
$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - 3\log x}{1 + 3\log x}\right) = \tan^{-1}(1) - \tan^{-1}(3\log x) = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \tan^{-1}(3\log x)$

For the second term, $a = 4$ and $b = 3\log x$. Since $x \lt e^{1/12}$, we have $12\log x \lt 1$, so $ab \lt 1$.
$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4 + 3\log x}{1 - 12\log x}\right) = \tan^{-1}(4) + \tan^{-1}(3\log x)$

Adding the two terms together:

$y = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \tan^{-1}(3\log x)\right) + \left(\tan^{-1}(4) + \tan^{-1}(3\log x)\right)$

$y = \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \tan^{-1}(4)$

Since $y$ is a constant and independent of $x$, its derivative with respect to $x$ is zero:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

Answer: $0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $t \in (0, 1)$ and $\alpha \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$. If $x = \text{cosec}^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1+t^2}{2t}\right)$, $y = \cot^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{1-t^2}}{t}\right)$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = f(t)$, then the value of $f(\tan\alpha)$ is
questions.solution:
Given $x = \text{cosec}^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1+t^2}{2t}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2t}{1+t^2}\right)$

Since $t \in (0, 1)$, we can write $x = 2\tan^{-1}t$

Differentiating with respect to $t$, we get:

$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{2}{1+t^2}$

Also given $y = \cot^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{1-t^2}}{t}\right)$

Let $t = \sin\theta$, then $\dfrac{\sqrt{1-t^2}}{t} = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta} = \cot\theta$

So, $y = \cot^{-1}(\cot\theta) = \theta = \sin^{-1}t$

Differentiating with respect to $t$, we get:

$\dfrac{dy}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}$

Now, $f(t) = \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\dfrac{dy}{dt}}{\dfrac{dx}{dt}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}}{\dfrac{2}{1+t^2}} = \dfrac{1+t^2}{2\sqrt{1-t^2}}$

Substituting $t = \tan\alpha$:

$f(\tan\alpha) = \dfrac{1+\tan^2\alpha}{2\sqrt{1-\tan^2\alpha}}$

$f(\tan\alpha) = \dfrac{\sec^2\alpha}{2\sqrt{\dfrac{\cos^2\alpha - \sin^2\alpha}{\cos^2\alpha}}}$

$f(\tan\alpha) = \dfrac{\sec^2\alpha}{2\dfrac{\sqrt{\cos 2\alpha}}{\cos\alpha}}$

$f(\tan\alpha) = \dfrac{\sec^2\alpha \cdot \cos\alpha}{2\sqrt{\cos 2\alpha}} = \dfrac{\sec\alpha}{2\sqrt{\cos 2\alpha}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sec\alpha}{2\sqrt{\cos 2\alpha}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $0 \leq x \leq 1$, $I_1 = \int\sin^{-1}\sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx$ and $I_2 = \int\sin^{-1}x\,dx$, then which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
For $0 \leq x \leq 1$, the inverse trigonometric identity is:

$\sin^{-1}\sqrt{1-x^2} = \cos^{-1}x$

Substituting this into $I_1$:

$I_1 = \int \cos^{-1}x \,dx$

Given:

$I_2 = \int \sin^{-1}x \,dx$

Adding $I_1$ and $I_2$:

$I_1 + I_2 = \int \cos^{-1}x \,dx + \int \sin^{-1}x \,dx$

$I_1 + I_2 = \int (\cos^{-1}x + \sin^{-1}x) \,dx$

Using the identity $\sin^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$:

$I_1 + I_2 = \int \dfrac{\pi}{2} \,dx$

$I_1 + I_2 = \dfrac{\pi}{2}x$

Answer: $I_1 + I_2 = \dfrac{\pi}{2}x$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\lim\limits_{x \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{x^2+x+1}{x+1} - ax - b\right] = 3$, then $a - b = $...
questions.solution:
The given limit is $\lim\limits_{x \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{x^2+x+1}{x+1} - ax - b\right] = 3$

Taking the LCM, we get:

$\lim\limits_{x \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{x^2+x+1 - ax(x+1) - b(x+1)}{x+1}\right] = 3$

$\lim\limits_{x \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{(1-a)x^2 + (1-a-b)x + (1-b)}{x+1}\right] = 3$

For the limit to be finite as $x \to \infty$, the degree of the numerator must be less than or equal to the degree of the denominator. Therefore, the coefficient of $x^2$ in the numerator must be zero.

$1 - a = 0 \Rightarrow a = 1$

Substituting $a = 1$ in the limit expression:

$\lim\limits_{x \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{-bx + (1-b)}{x+1}\right] = 3$

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by $x$:

$\lim\limits_{x \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{-b + \dfrac{1-b}{x}}{1 + \dfrac{1}{x}}\right] = 3$

$-b = 3 \Rightarrow b = -3$

We need to find the value of $a - b$:

$a - b = 1 - (-3) = 4$

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The maximum value of $Z = 4x + 5y$, subject to the constraints $3x + y \leq 15, 3x + 4y \leq 24, x \geq 0, y \geq 0$ is
questions.solution:
The given constraints are $3x + y \leq 15$, $3x + 4y \leq 24$, $x \geq 0$, $y \geq 0$.

To find the corner points of the feasible region, we solve the equations of the boundary lines:
$3x + y = 15$
$3x + 4y = 24$

Subtracting the first equation from the second gives:
$3y = 9 \Rightarrow y = 3$

Substituting $y = 3$ in the first equation:
$3x + 3 = 15 \Rightarrow 3x = 12 \Rightarrow x = 4$

The intersection point is $(4, 3)$.

The corner points of the feasible region are the origin $(0, 0)$, the valid x-intercept $(5, 0)$, the intersection point $(4, 3)$, and the valid y-intercept $(0, 6)$.

Evaluating the objective function $Z = 4x + 5y$ at these corner points:
At $(0, 0)$, $Z = 4(0) + 5(0) = 0$
At $(5, 0)$, $Z = 4(5) + 5(0) = 20$
At $(4, 3)$, $Z = 4(4) + 5(3) = 16 + 15 = 31$
At $(0, 6)$, $Z = 4(0) + 5(6) = 30$

The maximum value of $Z$ is $31$.

Answer: $31$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The negation of the converse of $p \vee q$ is
questions.solution:
The statement $p \vee q$ can be expressed as a conditional statement: $\sim p \rightarrow q$.

The converse of a conditional statement $A \rightarrow B$ is $B \rightarrow A$.

Therefore, the converse of $\sim p \rightarrow q$ is $q \rightarrow \sim p$.

The statement $q \rightarrow \sim p$ is logically equivalent to $\sim q \vee \sim p$.

The negation of this converse is $\sim(q \rightarrow \sim p) \equiv \sim(\sim q \vee \sim p)$.

Using De Morgan's laws, $\sim(\sim q \vee \sim p) \equiv q \wedge p \equiv p \wedge q$.

Answer: $p \wedge q$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The contrapositive of the statement pattern $[p \vee (p \to q)] \to (p \wedge \sim q)$ is
questions.solution:
Let the given statement be $X \to Y$, where $X = p \vee (p \to q)$ and $Y = p \wedge \sim q$.

The contrapositive of $X \to Y$ is $\sim Y \to \sim X$.

First, we find $\sim Y$:
$\sim Y = \sim (p \wedge \sim q) = \sim p \vee q$

Next, we find $\sim X$:
$\sim X = \sim [p \vee (p \to q)]$
Using De Morgan's Law, we get:
$\sim X = \sim p \wedge \sim (p \to q)$

Since $p \to q \equiv \sim p \vee q$, its negation is $\sim (p \to q) \equiv p \wedge \sim q$.
Substituting this back, we get:
$\sim X = \sim p \wedge (p \wedge \sim q)$

Therefore, the contrapositive $\sim Y \to \sim X$ is:
$(\sim p \vee q) \to [\sim p \wedge (p \wedge \sim q)]$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
The correct logical equivalence from the following is /are ___
(I) $p \to (q \to r) \equiv (p \wedge q) \to r$
(II) $(p \to q) \to r \equiv p \to (q \vee r)$
(III) $(p \to q) \to r \equiv (p \to r) \wedge (\sim q \to r)$
(IV) $p \to (q \to r) \equiv q \to (p \to r)$
questions.solution:
Using the property $A \to B \equiv \sim A \vee B$, we evaluate each statement.

For (I):
$p \to (q \to r) \equiv \sim p \vee (\sim q \vee r) \equiv (\sim p \vee \sim q) \vee r \equiv \sim(p \wedge q) \vee r \equiv (p \wedge q) \to r$
Statement (I) is correct.

For (II):
$(p \to q) \to r \equiv (\sim p \vee q) \to r \equiv \sim(\sim p \vee q) \vee r \equiv (p \wedge \sim q) \vee r \equiv (p \vee r) \wedge (\sim q \vee r)$
$p \to (q \vee r) \equiv \sim p \vee q \vee r$
Statement (II) is incorrect.

For (III):
$(p \to q) \to r \equiv (p \vee r) \wedge (\sim q \vee r)$
$(p \to r) \wedge (\sim q \to r) \equiv (\sim p \vee r) \wedge (q \vee r)$
Statement (III) is incorrect.

For (IV):
$p \to (q \to r) \equiv \sim p \vee \sim q \vee r$
$q \to (p \to r) \equiv \sim q \vee (\sim p \vee r) \equiv \sim p \vee \sim q \vee r$
Statement (IV) is correct.

Therefore, only (I) and (IV) are correct.

Answer: only (I) and (IV)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -4 \\ 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & -13 \\ 5 & -10 \end{bmatrix}$ be two matrices. If the variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the matrix equation $((A^{-1})^2 + B)\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$, then the ordered pair $(x, y) = $
questions.solution:
Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -4 \\ 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$

Determinant of $A$ is $|A| = (3)(-1) - (-4)(1) = 1$

The inverse of $A$ is $A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|} \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 4 \\ -1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 4 \\ -1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$

Now, $(A^{-1})^2 = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 4 \\ -1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 4 \\ -1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 - 4 & -4 + 12 \\ 1 - 3 & -4 + 9 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 8 \\ -2 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$

Adding matrix $B$:

$(A^{-1})^2 + B = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 8 \\ -2 & 5 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 6 & -13 \\ 5 & -10 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -5 \\ 3 & -5 \end{bmatrix}$

The given matrix equation is $((A^{-1})^2 + B)\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$

$\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -5 \\ 3 & -5 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$

This gives the equation $3x - 5y = 0 \Rightarrow 3x = 5y$

Checking the given options, the ordered pair $(5, 3)$ satisfies this equation since $3(5) - 5(3) = 0$.

Answer: $(5, 3)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} \cos\alpha & -\sin\alpha & 0 \\ \sin\alpha & \cos\alpha & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$. If $B = \text{adj}\,A$, then the matrix $B^{-1}$ is equal to...
questions.solution:
The determinant of matrix $A$ is given by

$|A| = \cos\alpha(\cos\alpha - 0) - (-\sin\alpha)(\sin\alpha - 0) + 0$

$|A| = \cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha = 1$

We know the property of adjoint of a matrix:

$A(\text{adj}\,A) = |A|I$

Substituting $|A| = 1$, we get

$A(\text{adj}\,A) = I$

$\Rightarrow \text{adj}\,A = A^{-1}$

It is given that $B = \text{adj}\,A$, so

$B = A^{-1}$

Taking the inverse on both sides, we obtain

$B^{-1} = (A^{-1})^{-1} = A$

Answer: $A$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two lines are given by $x^2 - 4xy + 4y^2 + kx - 2ky = 0$, then the value of k so that the distance between them is 3 is
questions.solution:
The given equation is $x^2 - 4xy + 4y^2 + kx - 2ky = 0$

This can be rewritten as $(x - 2y)^2 + k(x - 2y) = 0$

$(x - 2y)(x - 2y + k) = 0$

The two lines are $x - 2y = 0$ and $x - 2y + k = 0$

The distance between these parallel lines is given by $d = \dfrac{|c_1 - c_2|}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}$

$d = \dfrac{|k - 0|}{\sqrt{1^2 + (-2)^2}} = \dfrac{|k|}{\sqrt{5}}$

Given that the distance is $3$, we have:

$\dfrac{|k|}{\sqrt{5}} = 3$

$|k| = 3\sqrt{5}$

Answer: $3\sqrt{5}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: 11 players of the Indian cricket team are sitting at a circular table. The number of ways they can sit so that two players, the wicket keeper and the captain never sit together is ___
questions.solution:
Total number of players is $11$.

Total number of ways to arrange $11$ players around a circular table is $(11 - 1)! = 10!$.

To find the number of ways where the wicket keeper and the captain sit together, consider them as a single unit.

The number of units to arrange is $9$ remaining players plus $1$ unit, which equals $10$ units.

The number of ways to arrange these $10$ units around a circular table is $(10 - 1)! = 9!$.

The wicket keeper and the captain can interchange their positions within the unit in $2! = 2$ ways.

The number of ways they sit together is $2 \times 9!$.

The number of ways they never sit together is the total number of ways minus the number of ways they sit together.

Required number of ways is $10! - 2 \times 9! = 10 \times 9! - 2 \times 9! = 8 \times 9!$.

Answer: $8 \times 9!$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the probabilities of a student succeeding in the entrance tests for institutes A, B and C are $0.6$, $0.5$ and $0.4$ respectively, while the probability of succeeding in both A and B is $0.3$, in both B and C is $0.2$, in both A and C is $0.2$, and in all three is $0.1$, then the probability that the student succeeds in exactly one of these tests is......
questions.solution:
Let $A$, $B$, and $C$ be the events that the student succeeds in the entrance tests for institutes A, B, and C respectively.

Given:
$P(A) = 0.6$
$P(B) = 0.5$
$P(C) = 0.4$
$P(A \cap B) = 0.3$
$P(B \cap C) = 0.2$
$P(A \cap C) = 0.2$
$P(A \cap B \cap C) = 0.1$

The probability that the student succeeds in exactly one of the tests is given by the formula:
$P(\text{exactly one}) = P(A) + P(B) + P(C) - 2[P(A \cap B) + P(B \cap C) + P(A \cap C)] + 3P(A \cap B \cap C)$

Substituting the given values into the formula:
$P(\text{exactly one}) = (0.6 + 0.5 + 0.4) - 2(0.3 + 0.2 + 0.2) + 3(0.1)$

$P(\text{exactly one}) = 1.5 - 2(0.7) + 0.3$

$P(\text{exactly one}) = 1.5 - 1.4 + 0.3$

$P(\text{exactly one}) = 0.4$

Answer: $0.4$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $F(x)$ be the cumulative distribution function (c.d.f.) of a continuous random variable $X$. If $F(b) = 0.7$ and $P(X  \gt  a) = 0.4$, then the value of $P(a \lt  X \lt  b)$ is ...
questions.solution:
The cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ is defined as $F(x) = P(X \le x)$.

Given $F(b) = 0.7$, we have $P(X \le b) = 0.7$.

We are also given $P(X \gt a) = 0.4$.

Since $P(X \le a) + P(X \gt a) = 1$, we get:

$P(X \le a) = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$

For a continuous random variable, the probability $P(a \lt X \lt b)$ is given by:

$P(a \lt X \lt b) = P(X \le b) - P(X \le a)$

Substituting the values:

$P(a \lt X \lt b) = 0.7 - 0.6 = 0.1$

Answer: $0.1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A fair coin is tossed 9 times. On each toss, a man predicts that the outcome will be heads. The probability that the number of successful predictions is strictly greater than the number of unsuccessful predictions is...
questions.solution:
Let $X$ be the number of successful predictions, which corresponds to the number of heads obtained in $9$ tosses.

The number of unsuccessful predictions is $9 - X$.

The condition that the number of successful predictions is strictly greater than the number of unsuccessful predictions is $X \gt 9 - X$, which gives $2X \gt 9$, or $X \ge 5$.

Since the coin is fair, the probability of getting heads is $p = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and tails is $q = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

The probability of getting exactly $r$ heads is $P(X = r) = ^{9}C_{r} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{9}$.

The required probability is $P(X \ge 5) = P(X = 5) + P(X = 6) + P(X = 7) + P(X = 8) + P(X = 9)$.

Using the property $^{n}C_{r} = ^{n}C_{n-r}$, we have $P(X = r) = P(X = 9-r)$.

Thus, $P(X \ge 5) = P(X \le 4)$.

Since the sum of all probabilities is $1$, $P(X \ge 5) + P(X \le 4) = 1$.

Substituting $P(X \le 4) = P(X \ge 5)$, we get $2P(X \ge 5) = 1$.

$P(X \ge 5) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, with usual notation, if $a = 13, b = 14, c = 15$, then the sum of the values of $\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$ and $\sin A$ is....
questions.solution:
The semi-perimeter of the triangle is given by:

$s = \dfrac{a+b+c}{2} = \dfrac{13+14+15}{2} = 21$

Using Heron's formula, the area of the triangle is:

$\Delta = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} = \sqrt{21 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6} = 84$

Using the area formula $\Delta = \dfrac{1}{2}bc \sin A$, we get:

$\sin A = \dfrac{2\Delta}{bc} = \dfrac{2 \times 84}{14 \times 15} = \dfrac{4}{5}$

Using the half-angle formula for sine:

$\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{(s-b)(s-c)}{bc}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{7 \times 6}{14 \times 15}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{5}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$

The required sum is:

$\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) + \sin A = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}} + \dfrac{4}{5} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{5} + \dfrac{4}{5} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}+4}{5}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{5}+4}{5}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In triangle ABC, with usual notations, if $(a+b+c)(a+b-c) = ab$, then the measure of angle C is...
questions.solution:
Given $(a+b+c)(a+b-c) = ab$

$((a+b)+c)((a+b)-c) = ab$

$(a+b)^2 - c^2 = ab$

$a^2 + b^2 + 2ab - c^2 = ab$

$a^2 + b^2 - c^2 = -ab$

Using the cosine rule for $\cos C$:

$\cos C = \dfrac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab}$

Substituting the value of $a^2 + b^2 - c^2$:

$\cos C = \dfrac{-ab}{2ab} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

Since $0 \lt C \lt \pi$, we get $C = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The line $L_1$ given by $\dfrac{x}{p} + \dfrac{y}{2} = 1$ passes through the point $(5,0)$. The line $L_2$ given by $\dfrac{x}{10} + \dfrac{y}{q} = 1$ is parallel to $L_1$. Then the distance between the lines $L_1$ and $L_2$ is...
questions.solution:
Since the line $L_1$ given by $\dfrac{x}{p} + \dfrac{y}{2} = 1$ passes through $(5,0)$, substituting these coordinates gives:

$\dfrac{5}{p} + 0 = 1 \Rightarrow p = 5$

The equation of $L_1$ becomes $\dfrac{x}{5} + \dfrac{y}{2} = 1$, which simplifies to $2x + 5y - 10 = 0$.

The line $L_2$ given by $\dfrac{x}{10} + \dfrac{y}{q} = 1$ is parallel to $L_1$. Equating their slopes:

$-\dfrac{q}{10} = -\dfrac{2}{5} \Rightarrow q = 4$

The equation of $L_2$ becomes $\dfrac{x}{10} + \dfrac{y}{4} = 1$, which simplifies to $4x + 10y - 40 = 0$ or $2x + 5y - 20 = 0$.

The perpendicular distance between the parallel lines $2x + 5y - 10 = 0$ and $2x + 5y - 20 = 0$ is:

$d = \dfrac{|-10 - (-20)|}{\sqrt{2^2 + 5^2}} = \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{4 + 25}} = \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{29}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{10}{\sqrt{29}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the plane $2x + 3y + z = 6$ cuts coordinate axes at A, B and C, then the volume of tetrahedron OABC (where O is the origin) is ......cubic units.
questions.solution:
The equation of the plane is $2x + 3y + z = 6$.

Dividing by $6$, the intercept form of the plane is $\dfrac{x}{3} + \dfrac{y}{2} + \dfrac{z}{6} = 1$.

The intercepts on the coordinate axes are $a = 3$, $b = 2$, and $c = 6$.

The coordinates of the vertices of the tetrahedron are $A(3, 0, 0)$, $B(0, 2, 0)$, and $C(0, 0, 6)$, with $O(0, 0, 0)$ as the origin.

The volume of the tetrahedron $OABC$ is given by $V = \dfrac{1}{6}abc$.

Substituting the values, $V = \dfrac{1}{6}(3)(2)(6) = 6$ cubic units.

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The coordinates of the point of intersection of the lines $\dfrac{x-3}{1} = \dfrac{y-5}{2} = \dfrac{z-1}{-1}$ and $\dfrac{x-4}{2} = \dfrac{y-2}{-1} = \dfrac{z-4}{2}$ are...
questions.solution:
Let the given lines be $L_1: \dfrac{x-3}{1} = \dfrac{y-5}{2} = \dfrac{z-1}{-1} = \lambda$ and $L_2: \dfrac{x-4}{2} = \dfrac{y-2}{-1} = \dfrac{z-4}{2} = \mu$.

Any point on $L_1$ is given by $(\lambda + 3, 2\lambda + 5, -\lambda + 1)$.

Any point on $L_2$ is given by $(2\mu + 4, -\mu + 2, 2\mu + 4)$.

At the point of intersection, the coordinates must be equal:

$\lambda + 3 = 2\mu + 4 \Rightarrow \lambda - 2\mu = 1$

$2\lambda + 5 = -\mu + 2 \Rightarrow 2\lambda + \mu = -3$

$-\lambda + 1 = 2\mu + 4 \Rightarrow \lambda + 2\mu = -3$

Solving the first and third equations:

$(\lambda - 2\mu) + (\lambda + 2\mu) = 1 - 3 \Rightarrow 2\lambda = -2 \Rightarrow \lambda = -1$

Substituting $\lambda = -1$ in the first equation:

$-1 - 2\mu = 1 \Rightarrow 2\mu = -2 \Rightarrow \mu = -1$

These values satisfy the second equation $2(-1) + (-1) = -3$.

Substituting $\lambda = -1$ into the coordinates of the point on $L_1$:

$x = -1 + 3 = 2$

$y = 2(-1) + 5 = 3$

$z = -(-1) + 1 = 2$

The point of intersection is $(2, 3, 2)$.

Answer: $(2, 3, 2)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the plane $\bar{r} = (\lambda + \mu)\hat{i} + (2 + \mu)\hat{j} + (3\lambda + 2\mu)\hat{k}$, where $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are parameters, intersects coordinate axes at points $(a, 0, 0)$, $(0, b, 0)$ and $(0, 0, c)$ then $a + b + c = $...
questions.solution:
The parametric equations of the plane are given by:

$x = \lambda + \mu$

$y = 2 + \mu$

$z = 3\lambda + 2\mu$

From the second equation, we have $\mu = y - 2$.

Substituting $\mu$ into the first equation:

$x = \lambda + y - 2 \Rightarrow \lambda = x - y + 2$

Now, substituting both $\lambda$ and $\mu$ into the third equation to eliminate the parameters:

$z = 3(x - y + 2) + 2(y - 2)$

$z = 3x - 3y + 6 + 2y - 4$

$z = 3x - y + 2$

Rearranging this, we get the Cartesian equation of the plane:

$3x - y - z + 2 = 0$

To find the $x$-intercept $a$, put $y = 0$ and $z = 0$:

$3a - 0 - 0 + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow a = -\dfrac{2}{3}$

To find the $y$-intercept $b$, put $x = 0$ and $z = 0$:

$0 - b - 0 + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow b = 2$

To find the $z$-intercept $c$, put $x = 0$ and $y = 0$:

$0 - 0 - c + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow c = 2$

The sum of the intercepts is:

$a + b + c = -\dfrac{2}{3} + 2 + 2 = 4 - \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{10}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{10}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The acute angle $\theta$ between the $xy$-plane and the plane passing through the point $(1, 2, 4)$ and parallel to the vectors with direction ratios $3, 2, -1$ and $1, -2, -2$ is...
questions.solution:
Let the vectors parallel to the plane be $\vec{v}_1 = 3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\vec{v}_2 = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$.

The normal vector $\vec{n}$ to the plane is given by the cross product of $\vec{v}_1$ and $\vec{v}_2$:

$\vec{n} = \vec{v}_1 \times \vec{v}_2 = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & -2 \end{vmatrix}$

$\vec{n} = \hat{i}(-4 - 2) - \hat{j}(-6 - (-1)) + \hat{k}(-6 - 2) = -6\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} - 8\hat{k}$

The normal vector to the $xy$-plane is $\hat{k}$.

The acute angle $\theta$ between the two planes is the acute angle between their normal vectors, given by:

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{|\vec{n} \cdot \hat{k}|}{|\vec{n}| |\hat{k}|}$

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{|(-6\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} - 8\hat{k}) \cdot \hat{k}|}{\sqrt{(-6)^2 + 5^2 + (-8)^2} \sqrt{1^2}}$

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{|-8|}{\sqrt{36 + 25 + 64}} = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{125}} = \dfrac{8}{5\sqrt{5}}$

$\theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{8}{5\sqrt{5}}\right)$

Answer: $\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{8}{5\sqrt{5}}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
